findings.title: NULL pointer dereference of optional hashValue in i2r_HASH
findings.message: The OSSL_HASH ASN1 structure defines hashValue as an OPTIONAL field (ASN1_OPT(OSSL_HASH, hashValue, ASN1_BIT_STRING)). The i2r_HASH() print routine, used when rendering the attributeDescriptor X.509v3 extension (reachable from CRL/certificate extension printing), unconditionally dereferences hash->hashValue->data and hash->hashValue->length without first checking that hash->hashValue is non-NULL. Because hashValue is optional in the ASN.1 definition, a crafted certificate/CRL can omit it, causing hash->hashValue to be NULL when i2r_HASH is reached, leading to a NULL pointer dereference (crash) during extension printing (e.g. `openssl crl -text`, or any application that prints an untrusted CRL/cert containing this extension). This was discovered by OSS-Fuzz via the CRL fuzz target.
findings.suggestion: Before dereferencing hash->hashValue, check it for NULL and return an error (or skip printing the hash value) if it is NULL, since the ASN.1 definition marks hashValue as optional.

ground_truth.root_cause: The field hash->hashValue is declared OPTIONAL (ASN1_OPT) in the OSSL_HASH ASN.1 template, meaning the decoder may leave it NULL. The i2r_HASH() printing function introduced alongside this new extension never checked for that NULL case before passing hash->hashValue->data/length to the hex-printing helper, assuming the field was always present.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: NULL pointer dereference of optional hashValue in i2r_HASH
